extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying functional analysis (readers of Brezis)
extracted.subtask_description: Partial solutions and worked remarks for convex analysis / functional analysis exercises (Hahn–Banach, subdifferentials, convex hulls, operator perturbations, topological properties of dual balls). Targeted at students verifying proofs and learning standard arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal set in F must be a singleton
rubrics_metrics.description: If M0 is a maximal element of a family F (ordered by inclusion) then M0 cannot contain two distinct points. If a,b ∈ M0 with a ≠ b then Hahn–Banach yields f separating a and b; letting M1 = {x ∈ M0; ⟨f,x⟩ = max_{y∈M0} ⟨f,y⟩} one gets M0 ≤ M1 and by maximality M1 = M0, a contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a separating functional from Hahn–Banach, define the subset of maximizers of that functional inside M0, observe it strictly enlarges when two distinct points give different values, contradicting maximality.

rubrics_metrics.name: K equals closed convex hull of its extreme points (Krein–Milman style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let K1 be the closed convex hull of all extreme points of a compact convex set K. If a ∈ K \, K1 then a can be strictly separated from K1 by a hyperplane; the maximizer set B = {x ∈ K; ⟨f,x⟩ = max_{y∈K} ⟨f,y⟩} is an extreme set intersecting K1 = ∅ but must contain an extreme point of K, contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Hahn–Banach separation of {a} and K1, define the face B of K where the functional attains its maximum; use that faces contain extreme points to obtain the contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdifferential of an indicator function IC (normal cone descriptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ϕ = I_K the indicator of convex set K: ∂ϕ(x) is the outward normal cone at x. In particular, if K is a linear subspace then ∂ϕ(x) = K^⊥; if x ∈ Int K then ∂ϕ(x) = {0}; if x ∈ Boundary(K) then ∂ϕ(x) equals the usual outward normal cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret subdifferential of indicator as normal cone and apply geometric definitions; these identifications are standard and used repeatedly when separating epi and support sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of epiϕ yields a subgradient (finding a subgradient via Hahn–Banach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying Hahn–Banach (geometric form) to A = Int(epi ϕ) and B = [x0, ϕ(x0)] yields a functional and constants with k > 0, from which one deduces that −(1/k) f ∈ ∂ϕ(x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the interior of the epigraph from the point [x0,ϕ(x0)] in E×R; check the sign of the vertical coefficient k to ensure one obtains a genuine subgradient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact subgradient decomposition for sums under infimal-convolution condition
rubrics_metrics.description: If inf(˜ϕ + ˜ψ) = 0 (where ˜ denotes the Fenchel conjugate), then one can find g such that f0 − g ∈ ∂ϕ(x), g ∈ ∂ψ(x), hence f0 ∈ ∂ϕ(x) + ∂ψ(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use duality and existence of minimizers for the conjugate problem to split a given functional into two subgradients coming from ϕ and ψ respectively; this is an instance of the subdifferential sum inclusion under appropriate qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local uniform bound on norms of subgradients (Lipschitz-type inequality)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ satisfies ϕ(x) ≥ −k(∥x∥+C) on bounded balls then for every R>0 and x0 one obtains an M(R) with ∥f∥ ≤ (k∥x0∥+kR+C−ϕ(x0))/R for all f∈∂ϕ(x0). Letting R→∞ yields ∥f∥ ≤ k for all f∈∂ϕ(x0) and consequently ϕ(x) − ϕ(x0) ≥ −k∥x−x0∥ for all x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate ⟨f,x⟩ using the subgradient inequality and the growth bound on ϕ, choose radii R and let R→∞ to get uniform bounds on subgradient norms and derive global Lipschitz-type inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain of conjugate is norm-bounded: D(ϕ*) ⊂ k B_{E*}
rubrics_metrics.description: From the previous growth/subgradient bounds one deduces that D(ϕ*) (the effective domain of the convex conjugate) is contained in the ball of radius k in the dual: D(ϕ*) ⊂ k B_{E*}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate bounds on subgradients into bounds on dual variables: if f lies in D(ϕ*) then its norm is controlled by the linear growth constant k appearing in the primal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonzero normal at boundary is proportional to a subgradient of ϕ (scaling relation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ∈ ∂I_C(x) with ϕ(x) = 0 and f ≠ 0, then there exists λ>0 such that f ∈ λ ∂ϕ(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate Int(epi ϕ) and a half-space determined by f in E×R, obtain a functional (g,k) with k>0 and deduce that the spatial component g is a scalar multiple of f; conclude proportionality to a true subgradient of ϕ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ekeland-type approximate minimizer existence and variational inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complete nonempty set M and lower semicontinuous ψ with ψ ≥ 0 and some λ>0, there exists x1 ∈ M such that ψ(x) − ψ(x1) + λ ∥x − x1∥ ≥ 0 for all x ∈ M (an approximate minimizer satisfying a variational inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct M as the set of near-minimizers, apply completeness and l.s.c. properties and the argument in Part A to obtain the existence of x1. This is the standard Ekeland variational principle style conclusion used to produce perturbation-subgradient relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-order inclusion from variational inequality: 0 ∈ ∂(ω+θ)(x1) with ∂θ(x1)=λ B_{E*}
rubrics_metrics.description: With ω(x)=ψ(x)−ψ(x1) and θ(x)=λ∥x−x1∥ one has 0 ∈ ∂(ω+θ)(x1) and ∂θ(x1)=λ B_{E*}; hence 0 ∈ ∂ψ(x1) − f + λ B_{E*} (or similar inclusions depending on definitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate the variational inequality into a subdifferential inclusion using sum rule properties and the known subdifferential of the norm (a multiple of the dual unit ball).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations between domains and ranges of subdifferential and conjugate
rubrics_metrics.description: One has the inclusions D(ϕ) ⊂ D(∂ϕ), R(∂ϕ) ⊂ D(ϕ*), and D(ϕ*) ⊂ R(∂ϕ) (with the latter obtained via approximations: for any f0 ∈ D(ϕ*) and any ε>0 there exists x0 with f0 ∈ ∂_ε ϕ(x0), and hence for any λ>0 one can find f1 ∈ R(∂ϕ) with ∥f1 − f0∥ < λ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use approximation by ε-subgradients, Fenchel–Moreau duality arguments and lower semicontinuity properties of conjugates to move between domains and ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boundary points admit (approximate) supporting hyperplanes
rubrics_metrics.description: If x0 is a boundary point of a closed convex set C then for every ε>0 there exists a point a ∉ C with ∥a − x0∥ < ε; separating C and {a} by a closed hyperplane gives f0 ∈ E* with ∥f0∥ = 1 and f0 ∈ ∂_ε I_C(x0); in particular for small ε one gets a genuine supporting hyperplane at a nearby boundary point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce the separating functional for the perturbed point a and normalize; use smallness of ε to ensure nontriviality of the supporting functional and locate an actual support at a nearby point of C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone convergence and conjugation interchange for sequences of convex functions
rubrics_metrics.description: For monotone sequences of convex functions ϕ_n (nondecreasing) and ψ_n (nonincreasing) with suitable bounds one has pointwise limits ϕ_n ↑ θ and ψ_n ↓ ζ and conjugation relations (e.g., θ* and ζ* relate to limits of ϕ_n* and ψ_n*). In particular constructions using ϕ_{n+1} = 1/2(ϕ_n + ψ_n) yield convergence claims θ = ~θ etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply convexity, homogeneity arguments and pointwise monotone limits; use Fenchel conjugation properties and lower semicontinuity to pass to the limit in conjugates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closedness and perturbation estimate for operators with relative bound
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is closed, densely defined and B satisfies an inequality ∥Bu∥ ≤ k ∥Au∥ + C ∥u∥ for all u ∈ D(A) with k < 1, then A + B is closed and one obtains an estimate on the graph/resolvent distance: ρ(A, A + B) ≤ k + C (with variants under further hypotheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inequality to show Bun is Cauchy when (A+ B)u_n converges, deduce domain/closedness for A+B, and apply the stated sup/inf formulas for ρ(A,·) to obtain the bound.
